query: Starting from bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what single intervention could further reduce its lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to the unchanged material? Earlier studies examined heat transport in idealized fcc and bcc concentrated alloys using atomistic calculations, DFT coupled to analytical models, or Debye-based estimates. Most simulations treated perfect, defect-free bulk crystals, while experiments below 200 K inferred separate lattice and electronic contributions from thermal-conductivity and electrical-resistivity measurements. For HfNbTaTiZr, these contributions were estimated to have similar magnitudes from nearly 0 to 200 K; measurements from 300 to 1200 K instead concern a sample containing 1 wt.% oxygen, limiting direct comparison with the starting material. Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its physical mechanism, a quantitative or directional prediction relative to unchanged bulk HfNbTaTiZr, the temperature and material-state boundaries of the prediction, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that would falsify the hypothesis while separating lattice-mediated from electronic heat transport.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing oxygen into bulk HfNbTaTiZr will further reduce its lattice contribution to thermal conductivity relative to the unchanged material.
generation.conditions: temperature range from nearly 0 to 200 K
generation.mechanism: phonon scattering by oxygen-induced defects or disorder
generation.baseline: lattice thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr without oxygen
generation.uncertainty: exact amount of oxygen introduction and its effect on lattice thermal conductivity

falsification_experiment.design: measure thermal conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr with varying oxygen content using the 3ω method
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if introducing oxygen does not reduce lattice thermal conductivity, the hypothesis is falsified

Own digest: Paper card. Question: How do the phonon dynamics of the high-entropy alloy FeCoCrMnNi compare to those of glasses and complex metallic alloys (CMAs), and does it represent a unique class of materials?. System: Fe20Co20Cr20Mn20Ni20 (FeCoCrMnNi), a 5-element equiatomic FCC random solid solution. Processing: Polycrystalline samples produced by alloying high-purity elements in an inductively coupled high-frequency levitation furnace, slip-cast into a water-cooled copper mold, and annealed at 1200 °C for 48 h; single crystals grown via the Bridgman technique at 1340 °C with a solidification velocity of 50 mm/h under 200 mbar argon. Test conditions: Measurements performed at temperatures of 3, 15, 100, 200, and 300 K using inelastic neutron scattering (INS) and inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS); energy ranges up to 30 meV and wavevectors covering the Brillouin zone.
